title: Main-frame response streamed through shouldInterceptRequest renders progressively (gate=beacon)

results.condition: Progressive in WebView read blocks only: the first read takes the bytes that InputStream.available() reports, then the WebView fills each 2048-byte read before it passes bytes to the renderer, so a smaller flush waits for more bytes or the end of the body (block-1500 runs: 4 s stall)

IOS-P1: cookies (document.cookie, HttpOnly cookie sent on a same-origin fetch) after loadSimulatedRequest

results.condition: WebKit ignores the Set-Cookie field of the simulated response and does not share the native URLSession cookies; the SDK must put the cookies of its native fetch into the WKHTTPCookieStore of the web view (setCookie, wait for the completion) before loadSimulatedRequest. With this sync (CAP-I-11) the page has the native cookies with their attributes: document.cookie shows all but the HttpOnly one, and same-origin fetches send all. Cookies that the page sets (HttpOnly by fetch, script cookies) work and go with same-origin fetches.

results.condition: The page origin is rqlab://localhost:18443, not the https origin; document.cookie is empty and a script cannot set a cookie; WebKit does not store a Set-Cookie of the scheme handler response, so relative requests carry only the cookies of the app's own URLSession. https subresources load and carry the cookies of the https site (SameSite=None; Secure seen), but a script can read a cross-origin https response only with CORS for the rqlab origin.

Cookie sync between WKHTTPCookieStore and HTTPCookieStorage for HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite

results.condition: Sync works in both directions and keeps HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict/Lax (native HTTPCookieStorage -> WKHTTPCookieStore.setCookie before the load; getAllCookies -> HTTPCookieStorage before a native fetch); WebKit then hides HttpOnly from document.cookie and does not send a SameSite=Strict cookie on a top-level navigation that a cross-site page starts. Conditions: URLSession does not apply SameSite (a native fetch sends Strict and Lax cookies also with a cross-site mainDocumentURL), so the SDK must not use its native fetch for a navigation that a cross-site page started, or must filter the cookies itself; cross-site subresources and iframes of the web view get no cookies at all (WebKit third-party cookie blocking), whatever the sync; SameSite=None and no SameSite are not told apart by HTTPCookie.sameSitePolicy (the value differs by iOS version), so the SDK must not depend on that value.
